results.q: What is the difference between moral responsibility and legal resnposibility. Give example.
results.answer: Moral responsibility tends to be shared among many individuals, whereas causal, role, and legal responsibilities tend to be exclusive [1]. Moral responsibility focuses on what individuals should do in the future rather than assigning blame for a past event [1]. In contrast, legal responsibility means an individual or organization can be charged with a crime or liable for damages in a civil lawsuit [2]. An example of legal responsibility is strict liability, where a manufacturer can be found liable for damages even if the product met all safety standards and the manufacturer did nothing wrong [2]. An example of moral responsibility is when a software tester neglects to sufficiently test a new module, causing service outages; the tester is morally responsible for the harms caused even though the outages were not intended [3]. Another example is a hacker who installs a keystroke logging program in an attempt to steal passwords; the hacker is morally responsible for attempting to invade privacy even if the program fails to work [3].
